analysis:
No findings: this batch is documentation only, and no Swift or Go source was supplied to confirm the described behavior.

configuration.md units 8 and 9 (head lines 478-734) lie outside the changed range (head 180-186). They are unchanged context. They describe the prefix-cache controls under T-041: TTL capped at 1800 seconds (line 661), DEBUG-only key file (line 660), and the kill switch and memory opt-in (lines 653-654). Nothing here weakens the T-041 or SEC-035 posture.

protocol-messages.md changes:
- Line 854: an optional `detail` busy reason.
- Lines 877-896: a closed vocabulary of Autopilot download refusals.
- Line 1230: `hold_seconds` placement holds, which exempt a target from LRU and idle unload.
- Lines 1279-1294: prefetch_model for a build outside ordinary serving becomes an Autopilot download. It sends no models_update, never loads or advertises the build, and re-registers when idle.
- Line 1380: `selected_models` becomes the persisted selection plus verified cached catalog builds. It grows and shrinks under an unchanged revision.
- Lines 1391-1419: new consent-gated telemetry (capabilities, download_storage, adopted_models, held_models, busy_reasons, transition_stalls).
- Lines 1470-1486: a restart now recomputes the set from cache and catalog without a new consent step. Previously it reused the recorded inventory.

Security relevance:
- The coordinator is trusted. The new telemetry goes only to the coordinator; volume and timing metadata are not consumer-visible according to these docs.
- Downloads use the existing hash pipeline and count against max_models, max_storage_gb and a 50 GiB reserve, which limits T-016-style disk exhaustion.
- Observation-only inventory still requires a live lease before routing (T-052 separation is preserved per the docs).
- The consent broadening is an operator-policy change: saved consent now covers future catalog builds. The docs disclose it, and operators can opt out via `[backend.autopilot_downloads]`.

Open questions for integration and source passes:
- Whether AutopilotDownload.swift actually withholds models_update and ordinary `register.models` for downloaded builds, so they are not publicly routable.
- Whether the weight-hash verification and the never-load guarantee hold in code.
- Whether holds can pin memory indefinitely; the 86400 s bound is per the docs only.
- Whether `private_only` Macs refuse these downloads.
